method:
Omori-Utsu parameters for the largest independent sequences since 1990 (ComCat, as-served magnitudes).

Selection : ComCat events M >= 7.5 since 1990-01-01, largest first; an event is skipped if it lies inside the
            space-time window of a larger selected mainshock. The first 40 independent mainshocks are kept.
Window    : epicentral radius R = max(100 km, L), L = 10^(-2.44 + 0.59 M) (Wells & Coppersmith 1994, all types);
            depth within 100 km of the mainshock depth (since 0.6.0; monitorlib.depth_window); time 0-365 days
            after the mainshock.
Mcat      : MAXC + 0.2 of the sequence events in days 10-365 (never below 4.5).
Fit       : omori_fit_mct (seislib): Omori-Utsu MLE with the time-dependent completeness
            Mc(t) = max(Mcat, Mm - 4.5 - 0.75 log10 t) (Helmstetter et al. 2006; Page et al. 2016), b = b-positive of
            the sequence events at or above Mcat (1.0 if it cannot be estimated).
Synthetic : the check removes the early events with the fit's own selection rule (binned M >= Mc(t) - 0.05);
            before 0.6.0 it removed M < Mc(t), a stricter cut than the fit assumes, which biased p upwards.
Quality   : A = n >= 100, sigma_p <= 0.10, 0.5 <= p <= 2, no other event >= Mm - 0.5 in the window;
            B = n >= 50, sigma_p <= 0.20, 0.5 <= p <= 2.5; else C. 'contaminated' marks a second large event.
            c_resolved is False when c < 0.001 day or has no standard error: with a teleseismic catalogue
            (Mcat ~4.7) the earliest hours are missing and c is then not constrained; K and p remain usable.
            c is searched in [1e-4 day, 365 days]; c_at_bound marks a fit whose c ended at either bound (1e-4 day
            or the upper bound max(T2, 1 day)); sc is then null and the errors of K and p are those for c fixed
            there. sK includes the covariance of K with p and c.

sequences.place: 41 km SW of San Vicente de Cañete, Peru

bt_method:
Retrospective b-value before and after the 40 Omori sequences (ISC-GEM Mw). A description, not a forecast.

For every sequence in site/data/sequences.json (written by sequences.py) this adds one field, `bt`, with b in four
windows around the mainshock, inside the sequence circle (radius_km, all depths):

  pre_5y      : 5 years before the mainshock (mainshock excluded)
  pre_1y      : 1 year before
  post_0_30d  : 0-30 days after
  post_30_365d: 30-365 days after

Catalogue  : ISC-GEM Mw, the atlas b sample (1976-2021, direct Mw only: common.b_sample_mask). A window that is
             not fully inside 1976-2021 is left empty with a reason, so sequences from 2022 on have no values.
Threshold  : per event, thr_i = max(period/depth floor of the atlas, MAXC+0.2 of the window sample) and, after the
             mainshock, also Mc(t) = Mm - 4.5 - 0.75 log10(t days) (Helmstetter et al. 2006 form; its coefficients
             were derived for California and are an assumption at teleseismic scale).
Estimator  : binned maximum likelihood (Tinti & Mulargia 1987) with per-event thresholds (seislib.b_varmc),
             bootstrap 95 % percentile interval with the window Mc re-estimated in each replicate; b-positive
             (van der Elst 2021) on events above the floor as an incompleteness-robust check. Quality codes as in the atlas (A/B shown, C and insufficient masked).
Validation : the 2004 Sumatra direction test against Srivastava et al. (2021, arXiv:2108.06557, ISC mb, 92-100 E):
             b 1.04 in the five years before 2004, 1.14 after. Our replication uses ISC-GEM Mw in the same longitude
             band (13 S-11 N), 2000-2004 vs 2005-2009. Only the direction can be compared (mb vs Mw).

Writes the `bt` field into site/data/sequences.json and results/val_bt.json (summary and table rows).
